\section[reclamar]{reclamar — to complain; to claim}

\label{lesson:PT-C434-reclamar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for mould, then the Portuguese for dirt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: reclamar}
\textbf{reclamar} — \textquotedblleft{}to complain; to claim\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Reclamámos do barulho, mas ninguém fez nada.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We complained about the noise, but nobody did anything.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Reclamar de} — to complain about.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{reclamar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{reclāmāre} 'to cry out against' (EtymDB), built on \emph{clāmāre} 'to shout'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{reclamar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{reclamar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{reclamar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for mould, then the Portuguese for dirt, then say \emph{reclamar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does reclamar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To complain; to claim\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[a reclamação]{a reclamação — the complaint}

\label{lesson:PT-C434-reclamacao}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for dirt, then the Portuguese for to complain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a reclamação}
\textbf{a reclamação} — \textquotedblleft{}the complaint\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Fiz uma reclamação na receção.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I made a complaint at reception.}
\end{quote}

Every shop in Portugal must have \emph{o livro de reclamações}, the complaints book.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{reclamação} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{reclāmātiō} 'outcry' (EtymDB), built on \emph{clāmāre} 'to shout'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a reclamação}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a reclamação}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a reclamação}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for dirt, then the Portuguese for to complain, then say \emph{a reclamação} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does a reclamação mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The complaint\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[resmungar]{resmungar — to grumble, to mutter}

\label{lesson:PT-C434-resmungar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to complain, then the Portuguese for the complaint.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: resmungar}
\textbf{resmungar} — \textquotedblleft{}to grumble, to mutter\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O meu avô resmunga quando o café está frio.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My grandfather grumbles when the coffee is cold.}
\end{quote}

Said under your breath.

\begin{cousinweb}
The origin of \emph{resmungar} is not settled; EtymDB lists Spanish \emph{remusgar} as a cousin.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[lamentar]{lamentar — to regret, to be sorry about}

\label{lesson:PT-C434-lamentar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the complaint, then the Portuguese for to grumble.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: lamentar}
\textbf{lamentar} — \textquotedblleft{}to regret, to be sorry about\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O gerente lamentou muito o problema.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The manager was very sorry about the problem.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Lamento muito} — I am very sorry.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{lamentar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{lāmentārī} 'to wail, to lament' (EtymDB), on \emph{lāmentum} 'wailing'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a indemnização]{a indemnização — the compensation (money), the damages}

\label{lesson:PT-C434-indemnizacao}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to grumble, then the Portuguese for to regret.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a indemnização}
\textbf{a indemnização} — \textquotedblleft{}the compensation (money), the damages\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A companhia pagou uma indemnização pelo atraso.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The company paid compensation for the delay.}
\end{quote}

In Brazil: \emph{a indenização}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{indemnização} is built on \emph{indemnizar} 'to compensate', a learned formation on Latin \emph{indemnis} 'unharmed', from \emph{in-} 'not' and \emph{damnum} 'loss' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a indemnização}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a indemnização}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a indemnização}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to grumble, then the Portuguese for to regret, then say \emph{a indemnização} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
